sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: This topic covers s. 20–22 under the Indian Contract Act, 1872. Read the statutory scheme as a coherent allocation of rights, duties, conditions, defences and consequences.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body:

2. Identify the statutory trigger in s. 20–22.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: The asserting party ordinarily bears the initial burden on essential facts, subject to admissions and statutory presumptions. Electronic records should be authenticated and presented under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Check jurisdiction, limitation, arbitration or jurisdiction clauses, court fees and the exact relief. Verify the applicable Limitation Act Article and accrual date.

Mutual mistake of an essential fact makes the agreement void; mistake of Indian law does not ordinarily make a contract voidable; unilateral mistake of fact does not by itself make a contract voidable.

enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 20–22 distinguish mutual mistake of essential fact, mistake of law and unilateral mistake of fact. Mutual mistake of an essential fact makes the agreement void; mistake of Indian law does not ordinarily make a contract voidable; unilateral mistake of fact does not by itself make a contract voidable.

Definition: The mistake provisions allocate different legal consequences according to whether the mistake is mutual and essential, concerns law in force in India, or is unilateral.

Ingredients:
1. Identify the subject matter and alleged mistake.
2. For section 20, prove both parties were mistaken about an essential fact.
3. For section 21, identify whether the mistake concerns law in force in India or law outside India.
4. For section 22, recognise that unilateral mistake of fact alone does not make the contract voidable.
examples: A and B agree for sale of a specific cargo believed to be on its way; the cargo had already been lost and neither knew it. The statutory illustration treats the agreement as void under section 20.
